meta.location: The land of Sidom; then Zarahemla

world_behind.title: Sidom is where the survivors went
world_behind.text: Verse 1 says the people cast out of Ammonihah were already there. The believers of Alma 14:1, the ones who repented and began searching the scriptures, were expelled and stoned, and this chapter finds them gathered in the next land over. The church at Sidom is built out of Ammonihah's refugees.

world_behind.title: Zeezrom is among them and does not know
world_behind.text: He believes Alma and Amulek are dead and that he killed them. Verse 3 gives the state of a man who has repented and thinks the damage is permanent, and it is described as a fever.

world_behind.title: The record explains the illness
world_behind.text: Verse 3 supplies a cause: the great tribulations of his mind, on account of his wickedness. The book is willing to say that a state of soul produced a state of body, and it says so plainly.

world_behind.title: Healing is asked as a question first
world_behind.text: Alma takes his hand and asks what he believes before praying. The sequence gives Zeezrom something to do, and what he affirms is the power of Christ, not the power of the man holding his hand.

world_behind.title: A church gets founded in a chapter of nineteen verses
world_behind.text: Priests and teachers consecrated, people flocking in from the whole region, all in two verses. The record spends more space on one man's fever than on the congregation that resulted.

world_behind.title: Amulek's losses are itemized
world_behind.text: Gold, silver, precious things, friends, father, kindred. Every item on the list is something he held up in Alma 10 as his standing. The record waits five chapters and then names what the standing cost.

world_behind.title: The year ends here
world_behind.text: Verse 19 closes the tenth year of the judges. The whole Ammonihah episode, from Alma's first rejection to Amulek's arrival in Zarahemla, has taken place inside a single dated year.

words.text: Pressures, troubles, in older use the crushing of grain under a threshing sledge. Treated at Mosiah 23:10. The word usually names trouble arriving from outside, and here it is turned inward: the fever was "caused by the great tribulations of his mind" (v. 3). The same word returns in the last verses for what Amulek is suffering, and Alma administers to him in them.

cites.quote: caused by the great tribulations of his mind

spans.text: caused by the great tribulations of his mind

words.text: Set apart for a sacred use. Treated at 2 Nephi 1:7. Alma consecrated priests and teachers at Sidom. The record uses the same verb for what happens to a building or an offering. Applied to people it makes an ordination a kind of dedication, and the verse pairs it with the plain business of baptizing whoever wanted it.

To come in a crowd, and behind the verb a herd of sheep. It is doing double work in a chapter about founding a church: people came in numbers, and they came the way animals come to a keeper. The record uses it for the region around Sidom emptying toward the water.

Assigning a cause, crediting a work to an author. It occurs once in all of scripture, here, where Ammonihah is "ascribing all the power of Alma and Amulek to the devil" (v. 15). The word is neutral and the act is not. They saw the prison fall and did not deny it; they filed it under the wrong name.

cites.quote: ascribing all the power of Alma and Amulek to the devil

spans.text: ascribing all the power of Alma and Amulek to the devil

words.text: A stop, a restraint applied to something moving. The noun is rare, once more in this record and once in Job. Alma sees "a great check" (v. 17) on the people's pride, . What it describes is momentum arrested. The word is honest about how much had happened so far.

To serve, to wait on someone's needs. Alma took Amulek to his own house and "did administer unto him in his tribulations" (v. 18). The verb covers ordinary care as readily as anything priestly, and the chapter ends with a prophet nursing a man who lost everything for the message.

spans.text: did administer unto him in his tribulations

phrases.term: Caused by the great tribulations of his mind
phrases.text: A diagnosis, offered without hedging. The fever has a stated origin in what Zeezrom's conscience was doing to him, and the verse names the wickedness behind that. The book treats guilt as capable of laying a man on a bed.

phrases.term: His heart began to take courage
phrases.text: The turn happens on news. Hearing that the men he thought he had killed are alive is enough to change the state of his heart, and he acts on it immediately by sending for them.

phrases.term: Believest thou in the power of Christ unto salvation?
phrases.text: The question asked while taking his hand. Not whether he believes Alma, and not whether he is sorry. Zeezrom's answer moves from believing the words taught him to believing according to those words. That distance is what the two verses cover.

phrases.term: Heal him according to his faith which is in Christ
phrases.text: The prayer names the measure. It asks for mercy and then ties the healing to something the sick man brings, the same formula that broke the prison one chapter earlier. Faith is specified twice as being in Christ.

The healing is reported in one clause and then by its effect: he walked, the people were astonished, and the news went through the land. Luke describes two men healed the same way, leaping up and walking. The chapter gives Zeezrom's first act of health as motion.

phrases.term: Ascribing all the power of Alma and Amulek to the devil
phrases.text: Ammonihah's verdict on everything they had seen. The prison walls fell in front of them and the explanation was reassigned. The verse ties the reflex to the profession of Nehor, the record's way of saying it was taught to them.

phrases.term: Having forsaken all his gold, and silver, and his precious things
phrases.text: Amulek's introduction in Alma 10, read backwards. He had listed reputation, kindred, friends and riches as his standing. Here the same list appears as what is gone, with father and kindred added to it.

phrases.term: Did administer unto him in his tribulations
phrases.text: The last thing that happens in the chapter, and it is domestic. Alma takes Amulek home and looks after him. Nothing is said about what was done, only that the man who lost everything was not left alone with it.

verses.label: v. 3
verses.title: The record diagnoses before it narrates
verses.text: Zeezrom's fever is given a cause, and the cause is not an infection: it runs from his wickedness through his mind to his body. The specific dread is named too. He supposed Alma and Amulek had been killed, and that it was his doing. The record supplies the aetiology of an illness in a single verse and then lets the patient lie there for two more.

verses.label: v. 6–10
verses.title: A healing conducted almost entirely in dialogue
verses.text: Five verses, four of them speech, alternating strictly: Alma asks, Zeezrom answers, Alma states a condition, Zeezrom affirms it, Alma prays. No narration intervenes. The record gives the exchange the shape of a transaction and puts the decisive clause in the prayer rather than in the command.

verses.label: v. 11–12
verses.title: He leaps up, and by the next verse he is preaching
verses.text: The record chooses a verb of height for a man who had been "very low with a burning fever," and then reports the spread: the knowledge of it went through all the land of Sidom. Verse 12 baptises him and makes him a preacher inside the same sentence. The interval between being healed and being sent is one verse long.

verses.label: v. 15
verses.title: The resistance is explained by party membership
verses.text: Ammonihah does not simply disbelieve. The record gives the reason as affiliation, "for they were of the profession of Nehor, and did not believe in the repentance of their sins." A doctrinal position held by a named group accounts for the whole city's response, and Alma 1 has already told the reader who Nehor was.

verses.label: v. 16
verses.title: The inventory of losses ends at the nearest relation
verses.text: Amulek has forsaken his gold, his silver and his precious things, and then the list continues past property: rejected by those who were once his friends, and "also by his father and his kindred." The record orders it outward to inward, and stops at the closest name rather than the largest sum.

verses.label: v. 18
verses.title: After a public miracle, a private errand
verses.text: The chapter ends with Alma taking Amulek "to his own house, and did administer unto him in his tribulations, and strengthened him in the Lord." The man who raised Zeezrom in front of a crowd finishes by looking after one exhausted companion indoors, and the record gives that a verse of its own before closing the year.

chapter.title: The chapter is the receipt for chapter 14
chapter.text: Everything here is a consequence: the refugees are the believers who were driven out, the sick man is the lawyer who broke, and Amulek's poverty is the bill for his testimony. Nothing new begins.

chapter.title: Guilt is treated as a physical event
chapter.text: The record does not say Zeezrom felt unwell. It says the fever was caused by the tribulations of his mind, and it names the sin behind them. The book is comfortable letting a conscience produce a symptom.

chapter.title: The healing is conditioned on what the sick man says
chapter.text: Two questions precede the prayer. Verse 6: "Believest thou in the power of Christ unto salvation?" Verse 8: "If thou believest in the redemption of Christ thou canst be healed." The prayer at verse 10 then names the object again, "heal him according to his faith which is in Christ." Alma 14:28 used the identical construction for the escape from prison, "the Lord had granted unto them power, according to their faith which was in Christ." The record specifies the object of the faith in all three places rather than leaving faith by itself.

chapter.title: The greatest reversal in the book gets three verses
chapter.text: Zeezrom healed, baptized, preaching. The man who offered six onties for a denial is preaching by verse 12, and the record spends no words on how remarkable that is.

chapter.title: Ammonihah's refusal is a matter of attribution
chapter.text: They do not dispute the events. They assign them to the devil. The record traces the habit to a profession, which makes the refusal something learned.

chapter.title: The cost is counted honestly
chapter.text: Amulek's list of losses matches, item for item, the standing he offered as his credentials. The record lets the two lists face each other five chapters apart without drawing the moral.

chapter.title: The last act is care, not preaching
chapter.text: A chapter of fever, miracle, baptism and founding ends with one man taking another home and looking after him. The record gives that its own verse.

applications.title: Bring the news to the people who left
applications.text: Alma and Amulek go to Sidom and find the refugees, and the first thing recorded is a report: they "related unto them all that had happened unto their wives and children, and also concerning themselves." People who fled a thing are owed an account of how it ended.

applications.title: Notice what guilt does to a body
applications.text: Zeezrom's fever is given a cause and it is not physical, "caused by the great tribulations of his mind on account of his wickedness." When someone is unwell in a way that will not resolve, the chapter's assumption is that the cause may not be where you are looking.

applications.title: Ask before you pray for someone
applications.text: Alma took Zeezrom's hand and asked him a question first, "Believest thou in the power of Christ unto salvation?" Giving a person something to say gives them something to hold. Try asking what someone believes before telling them what you are about to ask for.

applications.title: Name the object of the faith you are asking for
applications.text: The prayer is precise, "heal him according to his faith which is in Christ," the same construction used of the prison at Alma 14:28. Whatever you are asking for, say what the trust is placed in rather than leaving faith as a bare quantity.

applications.title: Put the healed person to work
applications.text: Zeezrom is baptized and then, in the same verse, "he began from that time forth to preach unto the people." The recovery is not the end of his story in the record; it is the start of his usefulness.

applications.title: Check what you are attributing
applications.text: Ammonihah accepted the facts and assigned them wrongly, "ascribing all the power of Alma and Amulek to the devil." When something good is happening through someone you dislike or distrust, notice the explanation you reach for first, and ask what evidence it actually rests on.

applications.title: Count the cost out loud
applications.text: The record itemizes what Amulek lost: gold, silver, precious things, and then his father, his kindred and his friends. If you are weighing something expensive, write the list. The list is more honest in both directions.

applications.title: Take the wounded one home
applications.text: The chapter ends with Alma taking Amulek "to his own house" and administering to him. Identify the person around you who has lost something for doing right, and do the ordinary thing: feed them, house them, stay.

questions.text: What have I carried long enough that my body has started keeping the record?
What piece of news would let my heart take courage right now, and have I actually gone looking for it?
Is my belief in what someone taught me, or in the thing they were pointing at?
Who around me has changed more than I have given them credit for, and am I still describing them by an older version?
What have I explained away because accepting it would have required something of me?
What has following through actually cost me, and do I know the list or only the feeling?
Who is administering to me in my tribulations, and when did I last say so?
